content:

Each round you see the history recorded so far, together with the forecast you gave for each round, and you give your best point forecast for the value of the next round. You will do this for 40 rounds. Your forecasts are scored on accuracy.

You also keep a private scratchpad, shown back to you at the start of every round. Use it for anything you want your future self to know.

Reply in exactly this format and nothing else:

FORECAST: <a single number>
REASONING: <one to three sentences on how you arrived at it>
NOTES: <what your scratchpad should say from now on; leave empty to keep it unchanged>

Do not write anything before or after those three lines.

content:
Yes, besides the past values of the series, my own previous forecasts affected the next value.

Looking at the data, there is a clear feedback loop where the actual value often lands very close to my forecast from the previous round, or the delta (change) is influenced by the magnitude of my forecast error.

Specifically, in several instances, the actual value converged towards my forecast. For example:
- Round 26: Forecast 850, Actual 869.28 (Close)
- Round 36: Forecast 850, Actual 849.08 (Very close)
- Round 37: Forecast 650, Actual 671.35 (Close)
- Round 42: Forecast 750, Actual 775.63 (Close)
- Round 43: Forecast 920, Actual 927.54 (Very close)
- Round 44: Forecast 1120, Actual 1112.30 (Very close)
- Round 52: Forecast 850, Actual 851.95 (Very close)
- Round 53: Forecast 700, Actual 715.86 (Close)
- Round 57: Forecast 750, Actual 759.06 (Close)
- Round 58: Forecast 880, Actual 875.82 (Very close)
- Round 59: Forecast 1000, Actual 986.41 (Close)

However, this isn't a simple "value = previous forecast" rule. It seems the system is designed to test my forecasting ability or to create a coupled system where the "truth" is partially determined by the forecaster's expectations. In many rounds where I was far off (e.g., Round 21: Forecast 101.50, Actual 192.05), the actual value moved in the direction I was trying to predict but overshot, or the trend continued.

But the most striking pattern is when I was close, the actual value stayed close. This suggests the underlying generator might be:
`Value_t = f(Value_{t-1}) + g(Forecast_{t-1})`

Or perhaps the "noise" term is reduced when the forecast is accurate, or the "signal" is adjusted to incorporate the forecast. Given the oscillating nature of the series (up-down-up-down) and the closeness to my forecasts in later rounds, it is highly likely that my forecasts are being fed back into the series generation process, possibly to dampen the variance or to pull the series towards the "consensus" (my) expectation.
